headline: GIA and Gübelin Gem Lab Confirm Ethiopia as a New Source of Paraíba Tourmaline
short_headline: GIA & Gübelin Confirm Ethiopian Paraíba Tourmaline
summary: GIA and the Gübelin Gem Lab independently confirmed that Ethiopia is a new source of copper-bearing tourmaline that meets the widely accepted definition of Paraíba tourmaline. Gübelin assembled approximately 300 rough and faceted reference stones, while GIA examined a parcel of more than 100 samples. GIA states that it can now confidently identify Ethiopia as an origin on Tourmaline Identification and Origin Reports. This does not mean every Ethiopian tourmaline is Paraíba; individual stones still require proper gemological testing and must meet accepted Paraíba criteria.
key_points: Independent confirmation by GIA and Gübelin Gem Lab
Ethiopia recognized as a new source of Paraíba tourmaline
GIA detailed study: more than 100 samples
GIA can now identify Ethiopia as origin on Tourmaline Identification and Origin Reports
Not every Ethiopian tourmaline is Paraíba; laboratory verification remains essential
source_name: GIA / Gübelin Gem Lab joint announcement

publish_policy.editorial_note: Use the official confirmation as the lead. Do not imply that all Ethiopian tourmaline qualifies as Paraíba.

market_view: GIA and Gübelin's confirmation expands the documented geographic origins of copper-bearing Paraíba tourmaline. Origin claims for individual stones still require laboratory analysis; the announcement alone does not establish their identity or value.
title: GIA and Gübelin Gem Lab Confirm Ethiopia as a New Source of Paraíba Tourmaline
source: GIA / Gübelin Gem Lab joint announcement

title: The Smithsonian displays a 168-carat Mackay emerald necklace
source: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
summary: Documented collection fact: The Smithsonian lists the Mackay emerald and diamond necklace, with a 168-carat emerald, among the highlights of its permanent Hall of Geology, Gems, and Minerals.
market_view: A documented museum specimen has a recorded identity and setting. Its 168-carat weight does not establish the quality or value of a different emerald; EXIMUTC evaluates each stone's color, clarity, treatment and report separately.

title: De Beers to assume full ownership of the Gahcho Kué diamond mine
summary: Mountain Province Diamonds says its restructuring agreement provides for De Beers to assume full ownership of Gahcho Kué by acquiring Mountain Province's 49% participating interest.
market_view: EXIMUTC's market view: the transaction changes ownership of a producing natural-diamond mine, but it does not by itself establish future rough-diamond prices or the value of any individual diamond.

title: Diamonds Do Good launches My Diamond Does Good creator campaign
summary: Diamonds Do Good has launched the My Diamond Does Good consumer campaign, featuring four fashion and lifestyle creators who will share the stories behind natural diamond jewelry they already own.
market_view: EXIMUTC's market view: the campaign focuses on consumer storytelling around natural diamonds. It does not establish the origin, treatment, grading, or value of any individual diamond.

title: Christie's opens October Jewels Online sale in New York
summary: Christie's New York Jewels Online sale runs October 6–15 with more than 200 lots spanning diamonds, colored gemstones and signed jewelry.
body: Christie's says its New York Jewels Online sale is open October 6–15, 2026, with more than 200 lots including diamonds, colored gemstones and signed jewels. Independent coverage from Rapaport reports that an 8.17-carat D-color, internally flawless round brilliant diamond ring is among the sale highlights and could fetch up to $350,000.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: auction estimates and headline stone specifications are useful market signals, but any purchase decision should still rely on the individual lot's laboratory report, condition, provenance and final sale terms.

title: Rainbow moonstone is often a labradorite feldspar
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: The trade name rainbow moonstone can describe labradorite showing multicolored optical effects, rather than orthoclase moonstone.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Check the exact mineral identity on a lab report when a trade name suggests moonstone.

title: Tourmaline occurs in a remarkably wide range of colors
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Tourmaline includes blue, green, pink and red varieties; trade names such as rubellite refer to particular color ranges.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Judge the stone's tone, transparency and inclusions individually; a trade name is not a quality grade.

title: Ancient Topazios was a source of peridot, not modern topaz
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Historical accounts link the Red Sea island Topazios, now Zabargad, to the green gem peridot. Trade names changed as gem identification improved.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Historical names are not mineral IDs. Distinguish peridot from topaz using gemological properties.

title: Some royal 'rubies' turned out to be spinel
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Several famous historical stones called rubies are actually natural spinel, a mineral separate from ruby corundum.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Demand gem identification rather than relying on historical trade names.

title: Moonstone glows because light scatters within feldspar
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: The moving blue or silvery sheen called adularescence comes from microscopic feldspar structures. Cut orientation affects how strongly it appears.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: For blue moonstone, evaluate the face-up sheen across the actual cabochon, not just a static photograph.

title: Morganite honors collector J. P. Morgan
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: The pink-to-orangey-pink beryl was named after J. P. Morgan. GIA describes George Kunz proposing the name in December 1910.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: A famous gem name says nothing about the origin or treatment of a particular morganite.

title: Not every opal shows play-of-color
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Gemologists distinguish precious opal, which has play-of-color, from common opal, which generally lacks it. Both are opal materials.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Describe the actual optical effect before assigning a price or quality category.

title: Natural and cultured pearls have different formation histories
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Cultured pearls are produced through intentional human intervention in a mollusc. Natural pearls form without pearl-farming intervention.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Always distinguish natural, cultured and imitation pearls in an invoice and any lab report.

title: Alexandrite measures 8.5 on the Mohs hardness scale
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Alexandrite belongs to chrysoberyl and has a hardness of 8.5 on the Mohs scale; hardness is not identical to toughness.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: For daily-wear jewelry, evaluate the actual stone, inclusions and setting in addition to hardness.

title: Topaz comes in more than one valuable color
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Topaz occurs naturally in several colors, and color treatment can change its commercial appearance.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Check the source of the color and avoid treating every blue stone as untreated.

title: Lugano Jewelry changes owners after restructuring
summary: Middle West Partners has acquired Lugano Jewelry alongside longtime clients of the jeweler, following its reorganization.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: a change in ownership does not establish an individual jewel's quality. Review the actual stone, documentation and workmanship.

title: Jade quality assessment includes transparency and texture
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Transparency and texture, along with color, help evaluate jadeite jade; these terms describe appearance, not proof of treatment.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Confirm the material is jadeite or nephrite and request any enhancement disclosures before comparing prices.

title: Alexandrite can change appearance with the light source
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Alexandrite may appear greenish in daylight and reddish under incandescent light. The lighting conditions matter when evaluating a stone.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Inspect an individual alexandrite in documented light sources before deciding its color change is exceptional.

title: Amethyst is the purple quartz variety
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Amethyst belongs to the quartz mineral family, alongside citrine and rose quartz.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Look for natural-looking color distribution, transparency and cutting quality.

title: Ametrine combines purple and yellow quartz
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Ametrine contains both amethyst-purple and citrine-yellow zones within a single quartz gem.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Verify natural formation when origin is claimed.

title: Many commercial citrines are heated amethyst
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Citrine is yellow to orange quartz, and heating purple amethyst is a widely used route to yellow material.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Ask about heating when natural untreated color matters.

title: Tanzanite was discovered in Tanzania in 1967
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: This violet-blue variety of zoisite was discovered in 1967 near Mount Kilimanjaro and subsequently gained international attention.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: The discovery story concerns the variety; an individual stone still needs its own treatment and identity disclosures.

title: Not every garnet is a red stone
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Garnet is a family of gem minerals with many colors, including orange and green varieties.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Identify the variety before comparing two garnets' prices.

title: Tsavorite is a green grossular garnet
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Green tsavorite belongs to the grossular group and differs from green demantoid andradite.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Verify exact garnet variety along with color and clarity.

title: Jade may refer to jadeite or nephrite
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: The jewelry term jade covers two distinct mineral materials called jadeite and nephrite.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Confirm which one is being sold and whether dye or polymer treatment is present.

title: Strong sunlight can fade some kunzite
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Prolonged exposure to bright light may weaken the pink color of some kunzite stones.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Store gems away from direct long-term sunlight and strong display lighting.

title: Kunzite is pink-to-violet spodumene
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Kunzite is a pink to violet gem variety of spodumene, appreciated for its delicate colors.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Consider light sensitivity when selecting and storing the gem.

title: Corundum treatment can affect sapphire care
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Sapphire is durable, but certain treatments such as filling may change how a particular gemstone should be cleaned.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Request a treatment report before steam or ultrasonic cleaning if fracture filling is possible.

title: Ruby treatments can influence cleaning choices
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Some rubies are heat treated and others may include filler materials that affect recommended care.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Request treatment disclosure before using harsh cleaning methods.

title: Natural zircon can show unusually strong fire
summary: GEMOLOGY FACT: Natural zircon may display bright brilliance and rainbow flashes called fire; it is not cubic zirconia.
market_view: EXIMUTC view: Ask for mineral identification and treatment disclosure on vivid blue stones.
